note: Declared deltas of the native Claude roles (ADR 0037): a Semantic Core invariant that a native role does not bind in its body on purpose. Every other invariant is evidenced in the file (tests/helpers/native-invariant-evidence.ts). A delta is stale, and fails the suite, when the role's body does evidence the invariant.

deltas.feature: Check for delivered peer messages before the final report.
deltas.rationale: Tier-1 specialists stay hub-and-spoke (maintainer decision, plan 032 close-out, kept 2026-10-04): their body forbids messaging a sibling and routes every peer question through the lead, so there is no peer inbox to check. The lead relays and wakes.

deltas.feature: The handoff report lists peer messages received and open items.
deltas.rationale: The two sections are bound by the lead's brief (its template asks for `Peer messages received` and `Open items` in every report), not by the Tier-1 specialist's own body, which the maintainer chose to leave as it is.

deltas.feature: Message a peer directly only in team mode, when the brief lists that peer.
deltas.rationale: Stricter than the invariant: a Tier-1 specialist never messages a peer (its body says so), because team mode belongs to the Tier-2 packages on Agent Teams.

deltas.feature: At most two peer exchanges per specialist pair and one directed question per peer per planning round.
deltas.rationale: Stricter than the invariant: a Tier-1 reviewer or indexer holds no peer exchange at all, so the budget is zero.

deltas.feature: Component contracts settle through the orchestrator before touching peer-owned files.
deltas.rationale: The lead owns contract-first (it hands the contract as a fixed input before the slice starts); the specialist's body routes every question for a peer through the lead but does not name peer-owned files.
